posts.author: Lionbarrel
posts.body:
As I mentioned somewhere in these forums, I am an avid collector of old game media, digital or physical. And while I was in the deepest depths of my interest in RPG maker and its history, I came across some assets from a game I haven't heard of before and isn't mentioned in the RPG history timeline of their official website:
https://rpgmakerofficial.com/en/contents/history/
I remember a topic being mentioned of what RPG could do next as another entry in the series. And I've already left my first idea in the forum of this topic, which was to try other things out besides another sequel of basically the same thing.
Though side tangent; I didn't completely hate the idea of RPG maker/unity crossover, I believe what really hurt the sales or the market was the incident on unity side and there was no way of them predicting that that was going to happen...
This game was published roughly around the same time as RPG maker 2000/2k. RPG maker network was a diablo like engine that, I believe, had servers which made it multiplayer/MMO like,,, now I got this information from a Google translated article, so please forgive me if I got any of that information incorrect.
【歷史】消失在時代洪流的「Network RPG Maker 2000」 - 吹著魔笛的浮士德
西元 2000 年係網路遊戲開始蓬勃發展的黎明時期，ASCII 在 RPG Maker 2000 VALUE! 與 RPG Maker 2003 之間推出了支援網路同遊機能的「Network RPG Maker 2000」。
h9856.gameqb.net
Another interesting thing they did with this version of the game is that everything was isometric, unlike its typical top - down linear perspective from what we're used to. Characters like the hero players and the certain bosses were eight directional, well other things like simple monsters and NPCs for just 4 directional which were diagonal. Fascinating, and would love to see what other users would have done with it if it were as close as popular as the 2k3 and/or XP were.

posts.author: garahad-ser
posts.body: Yeah, I was quite surprised at just how many "maker" games they have released over the years.  As you probably know, they even released the old 1998 srpg assets for that particular maker, to go with the srpg plugins.

I know it's not the focus of your thread, but that's not really accurate. You can read through the extensive thread here about RPG Maker Unite - the "incident" (I presume you mean the pricing change) with Unity really had no effect on almost anyone who would be potentially publishing their games with Unite.
What killed it was the fact that it was released in a terribly under-developed state. The official game to demo the engine crashed when trying to be run; basic functionality wasn't included in the engine; tons of things didn't work correctly.

Do you recommend any sites as "best repositories" for old RPG maker games?  Regarding Unity - I think it was released too under-developed for standard users.  For actual amateur Unity users it is probably an amazing utility.  My Pre-Unite experience on Unity is following about a hundred tutorials to get an RPG framework up and running, then deciding it was too time consuming to master C# and complete a project.   I don't think it is a dead end, I just don't think it's going to appeal to the masses.
